chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) went out to perform the funeral prayer over one of their children, and upon him was a yellow al-khazz coat and a yellow al-khazz shawl.

key_terms.جُبَّة: A long outer coat or robe, worn over other garments
key_terms.خَزّ: Al-khazz: a fabric woven from a blend of silk and wool (or other animal fiber), distinct from pure silk, and permissible for men to wear
key_terms.صَفْرَاء/أَصْفَر: Yellow; the color of both garments
key_terms.مِطْرَف: A square shawl or cloak worn over the shoulders

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear al-khazz (silk-wool blend) garments in Islam?
ai.summary: Zurara reports that Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) led the funeral prayer for one of his children while wearing a yellow coat and shawl made of al-khazz fabric. Al-khazz is a permitted textile made from a blend of silk and wool — not pure silk — and this narration serves as evidence for the permissibility of wearing al-khazz garments, even in yellow, for men. The Imam's practice here demonstrates that wearing such clothing does not violate Islamic dress rulings.
